scene.ko: 아이와 함께 정전기 체험을 하며 안전한지 묻고, 아이의 질문을 대신 전해 쉬운 설명을 듣는다.

lines.en: Would your son like to try the static electricity ball? It makes your hair stand straight up.
lines.ko: 아드님도 정전기 공 체험을 해 보시겠어요? 머리카락이 쭈뼛 서요.

lines.en: He wants to, but he's a little nervous. Is it completely safe for kids?
lines.ko: 하고 싶어 하는데 좀 긴장했어요. 아이들한테 완전히 안전한가요?
alt: He'd like to, but he's a bit scared. Is it safe for children?
He's interested but nervous. Is it really safe for kids?

lines.en: It's totally safe. He might feel a tiny tingle, but it doesn't hurt. I'll be right next to him.
lines.ko: 완전히 안전해요. 살짝 찌릿할 수는 있지만 아프지 않아요. 제가 바로 옆에 있을게요.

lines.en: Okay, that makes me feel better. Go ahead, Minho. Just put your hand on the ball.
lines.ko: 네, 그러니 마음이 놓이네요. 해 봐, 민호야. 공에 손만 올려 봐.
alt: Okay, that's a relief. Go ahead, Minho. Put your hand on the ball.

lines.en: Look at that! His hair is going straight up.
lines.ko: 저것 좀 보세요! 머리카락이 쭉 서네요.

lines.en: Wow! He's asking why it happens. Could you explain it in a way a seven-year-old would understand?
lines.ko: 와! 왜 그런지 물어보네요. 일곱 살 아이도 알아듣게 설명해 주실 수 있어요?
alt: Wow! He wants to know why. Could you explain it simply for a seven-year-old?
Amazing! He's asking why. Can you explain it in simple words for him?

lines.en: Sure. Each hair gets the same kind of tiny charge, and things with the same charge push each other away. So the hairs try to get as far apart as they can.
lines.ko: 그럼요. 머리카락 하나하나에 같은 종류의 작은 전기가 생기는데, 같은 전기끼리는 서로 밀어내요. 그래서 머리카락들이 최대한 서로 멀어지려고 하는 거예요.

lines.en: So they're kind of like magnets that don't like each other. Did I get that right?
lines.ko: 그러니까 서로 싫어하는 자석 같은 거네요. 제가 맞게 이해했어요?
alt: So it's like magnets pushing each other away, right?
So they're like magnets that don't get along. Is that right?

lines.en: That's a great way to put it. You can even try it at home with a balloon and a wool sweater.
lines.ko: 아주 좋은 표현이에요. 집에서도 풍선이랑 털 스웨터로 해 볼 수 있어요.

lines.en: He'll love that. Thank you for being so patient with all our questions.
lines.ko: 아이가 정말 좋아하겠어요. 저희 질문에 하나하나 친절하게 답해 주셔서 고마워요.
alt: He'll really enjoy that. Thanks for patiently answering all our questions.
That's perfect for him. Thank you for being so patient with us.

expressions.note: 아이와 체험할 때 꼭 묻는 말

expressions.en: Could you explain it in a way ___ would understand?
That's a great way to put it.
